question.text: Chapter IX-A of SEBI LODR Regulations prescribes annual disclosures by NPOs registered on SSE. Which of the following is the CORRECT timeline for financial and non-financial annual disclosures?

answer.text: Financial: by October 31st OR before IT-return due date (whichever is later); Non-financial: within 60 days of FY-end.
Financial: within 30 days of FY-end; Non-financial: within 90 days of FY-end.
Financial: within 60 days of FY-end; Non-financial: within 180 days of FY-end.
Both financial and non-financial: within 30 days of the Annual General Meeting.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 3.2 of the chapter (citing LODR Chapter IX-A) states: financial aspects must be disclosed by October 31st of each year OR before the IT-return due date (whichever is LATER) or such other period as SEBI may specify; non-financial aspects must be disclosed within 60 days of FY-end or such other period as SEBI specifies. The SIA should calendar both dates distinctly. **The Trap:** Option A compresses both and drops the IT-return linkage. Option C doubles the non-financial window. Option D links to AGM — LODR IX-A uses FY-end and IT-return-due-date as reference points, NOT the AGM. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A/III-C (Compliance) test Reg 33 LODR (Main Board financials). XV (RA) uses audited financials in equity research reports. LODR Main Board has 45-day quarterly and 60-day annual; SSE IX-A has a different IT-linked date. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** For annual impact-report assurance engagements, align your reporting deliverable date with the 60-day non-financial limb — most SIAs underestimate this and deliver too late. Build a T-30/T-45/T-60 checklist and set the audit sign-off no later than T-55 to preserve a cushion.
